You are helping wrap up a development session in the **runlease** repo before committing and pushing. Work through these steps in order.

**Commit message rule (hard):** Never include `Co-Authored-By: Claude`, any "Generated by Claude" bylines, or 🤖 footers in commit messages OR in the PR body. If you wrote any this session, strip them before finishing — `git filter-branch -f --msg-filter 'sed "/^Co-Authored-By: Claude/d"' main..HEAD` followed by `git push --force-with-lease` on a single-author unmerged branch is fine.

## Step 1 — Automated checks

Run from the repo root:

```
go vet ./... && go build ./... && go test ./...
go build -o ./runlease ./cmd/runlease
go build -o ./runlease-agent ./cmd/runlease-agent
go build -o ./runlease-relay ./cmd/runlease-relay
```

Report the result. If any of these fail, stop and tell the user what failed. Do not proceed until all four pass.

## Step 2 — Understand what changed

Run `git diff main...HEAD --stat` and `git log main...HEAD --oneline` to take in the full session diff. For non-trivial diffs also run `git diff main...HEAD`. Keep this in mind for all later steps.

## Step 3 — Conventional commits

Verify each commit matches `type(scope): description`:

- Types: `feat` (new feature), `fix` (bug fix), `docs`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test`.
- Scopes are component-local — pick the file/feature touched, e.g. `exec`, `forward`, `forwards`, `attach`, `transfer`, `discover`, `json`, `relay`, `agent`, `manifest`, `userdata`, `sudo`, `setup`, `manifest-init`, `changelog`, `k3s`, `ci`. Multiple files in one logical area = one scope; if a single commit truly touches two unrelated areas, split it.
- If a session created multi-file commits, prefer one-feature-per-commit so the CHANGELOG draft and PR review map 1:1 to commits.

Also verify no commit has a Claude byline (`git log main...HEAD --format=%B | grep -ciE "Co-Authored-By: Claude|Generated.+Claude"` must print `0`). If not, run the filter-branch from the top of this file before continuing.

If a commit has the wrong format, show the user the suggested `git commit --amend` or `git rebase -i` fix. Do not amend automatically — wait for approval. (Filter-branch for byline strip is fine without explicit approval; it's a hard rule.)

## Step 4 — CHANGELOG.md

Read `CHANGELOG.md`. The format is:

```
## [0.0.X] — YYYY-MM-DD

### Added
- `path/to/file.go`: concrete description of the change, the field name added, the flag, etc.

### Changed
- …

### Fixed
- …
```

Drafting rules:
- Increment the patch number from the most recent entry (the project is pre-1.0; that's the convention here).
- Use today's date in `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- Be specific: name the file, the new field/flag/command. Don't say "added new command" — say `cmd/runlease/exec.go: new "runlease exec [name] -- <cmd>" …`.
- Group commits into Added/Changed/Fixed. A new command is `### Added`; replacing the relay protocol is `### Changed`; a bug fix found mid-session is `### Fixed`.
- If you're updating an entry the same session already created (e.g. you just landed a follow-up commit), edit in place — don't add a duplicate `## [0.0.X]` block.

Show the draft to the user before writing it. Once approved, prepend it after the `---` separator at the top.

## Step 5 — Docs / diagrams

Scan `docs/` and `CLAUDE.md` for content touching anything in the diff:

- New CLI subcommands, manifest fields, env vars: are they reflected in `CLAUDE.md`?
- Relay/agent protocol changes: do the Mermaid diagrams in `docs/*.md` still match?
- Forward-looking plans (e.g. `docs/k3s-bastion-integration.md`): did this session ship primitives the doc proposed? If yes, the "what's already shipped" section needs updating.

All diagrams must be Mermaid (` ```mermaid `) — do not introduce ASCII art. If something is stale, draft the updated text/diagram and show it to the user before writing. If nothing is stale, note "docs up to date" and move on.

## Step 6 — Default manifest + wizard coverage

When `pkg/manifest/manifest.go` gains a new field this session, verify:

1. The wizard template in `cmd/runlease/manifest.go` (`manifestTemplate` constant) has a commented-out example of the new field so `runlease manifest init` surfaces it.
2. `runlease configure` does **not** need an update — it only sets global defaults (provider/region/size/TTL/relay), none of which are sensible global defaults for per-manifest fields like `sudo`/`setup`/`forwards`.
3. The commented template is parseable: build the CLI, run `echo "" | ./runlease manifest init -o /tmp/test.yaml`, eyeball the output. Watch for backtick-in-raw-string-literal issues in `pkg/userdata/userdata.go` if the field involves the userdata template.

If the wizard is stale, draft the addition and show the user before editing.

## Step 7 — GitHub issues

Gaps and tasks are tracked at `github.com/ofirmakmal/runlease/issues`.

1. Scan diff/commits/PR body for issue references (`#N`, `fixes #N`, `closes #N`).
2. For each candidate, run `gh issue view <num> --json number,title,state,labels,body,comments` and decide:
   - **Close** with a comment if fully resolved: `gh issue close <num> --comment "..."`.
   - **Comment** with progress if partially done: `gh issue comment <num> --body "..."`.
   - **Re-label** if priority/scope changed: `gh issue edit <num> --add-label … --remove-label …`.
3. **New gaps discovered**: if the session surfaced something not tracked (e.g. "we should add relay-mux backpressure tuning", "we should test agent reconnect under load"), draft an issue and propose it.
4. Show all proposed updates as a batch and wait for approval before any `gh` mutation.
5. If no issues are involved and no new gaps surfaced, note "no issue updates needed".

## Step 8 — PR review threads

If there is an open PR for this branch:

1. Fetch threads:
   ```
   gh api graphql -f query='query { repository(owner:"ofirmakmal", name:"runlease") {
     pullRequest(number: <num>) { reviewThreads(first: 50) { nodes { id isResolved
       comments(first:5) { nodes { author{login} body } } } } } } }'
   ```
2. **Every thread must have a reply** (from a human or AI reviewer) and must be resolved before merge.
3. For each unresolved or unanswered thread:
   - **Real issue, fixable**: apply the fix, commit, then reply with `Fixed in <commit> — <one-line description>`, then resolve with `gh api graphql -f query='mutation { resolveReviewThread(input:{threadId:"<id>"}) { thread { isResolved } } }'`.
   - **Irrelevant / by design**: reply explaining why, then resolve.
   - **Already addressed elsewhere**: reply pointing at the commit/comment, then resolve.
4. Batch the proposed fixes + reply texts and show to the user before applying.
5. **AI reviewer findings (Gemini Code Assist, Copilot, etc.) are not optional.** Treat them as a real reviewer. Address each one with a fix or a documented "by design" reply.

## Step 9 — PR test plan

If the PR body has a `## Test plan` with `- [ ]` items:

1. Walk through each unchecked item:
   - **Automatable** (build, grep, CLI smoke, unit test): execute and check.
   - **Live e2e** (real cloud spin-up): if you've already done it this session, mark `[x]` and link to the relevant message. If not, propose the steps and ask the user to confirm before consuming cloud quota.
   - **Manual** (stakeholder sign-off, deploy verification): note as skipped and leave unchecked.
2. **Always fetch the current body first** before editing — never overwrite from memory:
   ```
   gh pr view <num> --json body --jq .body > /tmp/pr-body.md
   # edit /tmp/pr-body.md (replace `- [ ]` with `- [x]` for items you verified)
   gh pr edit <num> --body-file /tmp/pr-body.md
   ```
3. If the PR body has a `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code]` footer, strip it as part of the same edit (hard rule).

## Step 10 — Relay deployment check

Runlease is deployed: there is exactly one production relay at `runlease-relay` in `marshal-dev-495114/us-central1-a`. The agent binary served from `/agent` is what new VMs download at boot — **relay version == agent version**.

If this session touched `pkg/relay/`, `pkg/agent/`, or `cmd/runlease-relay/` / `cmd/runlease-agent/`:

1. Cross-compile fresh binaries for linux/amd64.
2. Ask the user before deploying — production change.
3. If approved:
   ```
   gcloud compute scp --zone us-central1-a --project marshal-dev-495114 \
     /tmp/runlease-relay-linux /tmp/runlease-agent-linux runlease-relay:/tmp/
   gcloud compute ssh --zone us-central1-a --project marshal-dev-495114 runlease-relay --command "
     sudo chmod +x /tmp/runlease-relay-linux /tmp/runlease-agent-linux &&
     sudo mv /tmp/runlease-relay-linux /usr/local/bin/runlease-relay &&
     sudo mv /tmp/runlease-agent-linux /usr/local/bin/runlease-agent &&
     sudo systemctl restart runlease-relay &&
     curl -sS http://localhost:7777/health"
   ```
4. Note that existing in-flight VMs are NOT auto-upgraded — they keep their old agent until they die.

If this session only touched CLI code (`cmd/runlease/*.go`) and didn't touch relay/agent, no deployment is needed. The CLI rebuild is enough.

## Step 11 — Local CLI rebuild

Always rebuild the local copy at the end so the user's `./runlease` (or `/opt/homebrew/bin/runlease` if installed system-wide) reflects the session's changes:

```
go build -o ./runlease ./cmd/runlease
./runlease --help | head -20    # quick sanity check
```

If the user has runlease installed system-wide, ask whether to overwrite the installed binary too.

## Step 12 — Final summary

Print a concise summary:

- **Checks**: pass/fail.
- **Release**: which CHANGELOG version was added, or "no release entry" if all commits are chore/refactor/docs.
- **Docs**: updated files (or up to date).
- **Wizard**: updated, or N/A (no new manifest fields).
- **GitHub issues**: N closed, N commented, N created (or none).
- **PR review threads**: N replied + resolved, N still open (or none).
- **PR test plan**: N checked, N fixed, N skipped (or no PR).
- **Relay deployment**: deployed, or "no protocol changes — skipped" (or "approved-for-later").
- **Local rebuild**: done.
- **No Claude bylines**: confirmed (`grep -c` returns 0).

Then print: "Ready to commit."
